# polyline.py

[简体中文](polyline.zh.md) ｜ **English** ｜ [← Back to README](../../README.en.md)

PolylineElement, created by pen.polyline.

## Classes and methods

### `PolylineElement`

Polyline element.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `bbox()` | Bounding box. |
| `set_points(value)` | Set points; the same as `update(points=value)`. |
| `get_points()` | Read the current raw points attribute. |

## Full example

Run it directly in PyCharm, or from the command line: `python malight/elements/polyline.py`

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os

    from malight import Malight, ColorName, StrokeJoin, StrokeCap, DashStyle

    _out = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__),
                                        "..", "..", "output"))
    pen = Malight(os.path.join(_out, "demo_polyline"), width=620, height=360)
    pen.set_background_color(ColorName.WHITESMOKE)

    # 1) Polyline: vertices joined in order, not closed with Z
    pen.polyline([(40, 280), (120, 80), (200, 280), (280, 80)],
                 fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.NAVY,
                 stroke_width=3, stroke_join=StrokeJoin.ROUND)

    # 2) A polyline can be filled: SVG closes it for the fill, the stroke stays open
    pen.polyline([(340, 280), (400, 100), (470, 240), (560, 120)],
                 fill_color=ColorName.KHAKI, stroke_color=ColorName.CHOCOLATE,
                 stroke_width=2, opacity=0.9)

    # 3) Wrap points into a shape: the stroke stays open, which suits open outlines
    pen.polyline([(60, 335), (160, 305), (260, 335), (160, 355)],
                 fill_color=ColorName.SKYBLUE,
                 stroke_color=ColorName.STEELBLUE, stroke_width=2)

    # 4) Polylines take the same cap and dash enums
    pen.polyline([(340, 340), (420, 315), (500, 345), (560, 320)],
                 fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.CRIMSON,
                 stroke_width=6, stroke_cap=StrokeCap.ROUND,
                 stroke_style=DashStyle.DASHED)

    # 5) Keep the element to restyle or measure it
    pl = pen.polyline([(300, 60), (360, 60), (360, 140), (300, 140)],
                      fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.TEAL,
                      stroke_width=4)
    pl.update(stroke_color=ColorName.INDIGO, stroke_width=6)
    print("polyline bbox:", tuple(round(v, 1) for v in pl.bbox()))
    print("polyline points:", pl.node.attribs.get("points"))

    # 6) The underlying data reads back as a vertex list
    print("vertices:", pl.points if hasattr(pl, "points") else "(see node.attribs)")

    pen.finish()
```
